Trust.title: Trust and safety
Trust.metaDescription: How Kvaterka.by tells a reliable host from a random listing: verification, reviews after a real stay, and dispute resolution.
Trust.lede: The main problem with renting isn't finding a place — it's whether you can trust this person. Everything below is built around that.

review.heading: A review can't be bought
review.p1: A review is tied to a specific completed booking: one from each side, and only if the stay actually happened. There's no way to write a review "just because" — no path exists that would get it into the database.
review.p2Rich: Both sides' reviews are published at the same time. Neither party can read the other's first and adjust their own, and neither can stay silent hoping the other will too: once the deadline passes, a lone review publishes on its own.
review.p3: A review shows the length of the stay, but never the exact dates. Publishing while a flat stood empty would create a safety problem.

tiers.heading: Verification tiers

basic.title: Basic
basic.body: Confirmed email address or phone number.

identity.title: Verified identity
identity.body: Requires a document — document submission is currently switched off pending a legal decision, and this tier isn't granted.

tiers.footerRich: A person makes the verification decision, it's logged with a reason, and the applicant is told the result. <link>Your verification status</link>.

rating.heading: The trust rating is explainable
rating.body: The profile page shows not just a number but what it's made of: how many completed stays, which confirmations exist, what the reviews say. An opaque automatic rating of a person is both a product mistake and a risk.

comms.heading: Conversations stay on the platform
comms.body: Before a booking is confirmed, messages stay inside Kvaterka, and attempts to take the conversation elsewhere are hidden — with an explanation to the sender of what was hidden and why. This isn't about retention: outside the platform there's no record of what was agreed and no way to resolve a dispute.

dispute.heading: If something goes wrong
dispute.body: A dispute can be opened from the booking card. A staff member reviews it using the message history and the check-in/check-out marks. The decision can't be rewritten after the fact — the action log is immutable even for administrators.

promise.heading: What we don't promise
promise.bodyRich: Moderator review of a listing is a review of the listing. We don't inspect flats, don't verify ownership, and don't guarantee that a place matches its photos. See the place in person before handing over any money.
